findings.evidence: #5–#7 'A little support · recognition practice … Name the problem clearly / Stay quiet and leave'.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Each repeat press gives a different, more concrete aid, such as a full sentence frame.

findings.title: Help did not give a sentence she could say
findings.expected: A usable frame such as 'The room is cold and…' for an A2 speaker.
findings.got: Only 'The room is…', a word gloss and a yes/no quiz; at #10 the starter was 'Yes, room twelve is good…' before any room was named.
findings.evidence: #4 'The room is…'; #10 'Yes, room twelve is good…'.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Starters match the scene facts and give a full sayable sentence.

findings.title: Recap shows an odd 'line hidden in this room'
findings.expected: A recap tied to what she said and where she needed help.
findings.got: The recap shows 'Name the problem clearly' as the 'line hidden in this room'. That is a quiz option, not a line from the scene.
findings.evidence: #15 'The line hidden in this room “Name the problem clearly”'.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Recap lists the phrase she was helped with, or her own coached sentence.

findings.title: Supported replies kept apart from independent ones
findings.got: Recap says '4 on your own · 2 with help' and the two helped turns are marked supported.
findings.evidence: #15 '6 spoken · 0 written replies · 4 on your own · 2 with help'.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Keep supported flags and the split in the recap.

findings.title: Held fixes are accurate and quote the learner exactly
findings.expected: Quote what she said and give a correct fix.
findings.got: Both fixes quote her words exactly and are correct.
findings.evidence: #15 'the heating is not work' → 'the heating is not working'; 'I go to room two one four now' → 'I am going to room 214 now'.

findings.title: Patient, in-scene help ladder with simple partner English
findings.got: The ladder runs gloss, then starter, then quiz without leaving the scene. Partner turns stay short.
findings.evidence: #2–#5 buttons 'Help me answer', 'More help', 'Choose a phrase'; partner 'Of course. Is that OK?'.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Keep short partner turns and help in the scene.

judge.voice: I liked that the hotel scene felt like my work, and nobody made me feel stupid when I pressed help again and again. The little hints were calm. But the help was thin. "The room is…" is not much, and the quiz about "stay quiet and leave" felt like a test, which I hate. Then I just said my own sentence anyway. The corrections at the end were right and I can use "I am going to room 214 now" at the desk, though I did not get to try it again. I wanted a second go with a new question, and it never came. I also like that it says honestly which answers had help. For my kids it looked safe. I would use it again for 15 minutes in the evening, but I would want that replay first.

prior.evidence: No moment and no replay in this run (#15); the gap's moment was never reached.
Both clear errors ('is not work', 'I go to room … now') were held and shown in the #15 recap.
#15 recap quotes 'I go to room two one four now', a real learner error, with a matching fix, not an unrelated first turn.
#5, #6 and #7 show the identical quiz 'What is the best first step?' on repeated presses.

verdictWhy.text: D2 failed: Help gave a gloss, 'The room is…' and an unrelated quiz (#5 'Stay quiet and leave'); she typed her own sentence at #7. Pause & coach never used; coaching is null, so no coaching note.
verdictWhy.check: The help actually unblocks the next reply; a coaching note quotes what they really said.

verdictWhy.text: D3 failed: No replay was offered or taken; moments is [] and the journey ended at the recap #15 with no fresh question.
verdictWhy.check: Replaying the moment gives them a fresh question, and they answer it better than before.
